scope: Global context, not HTAFL outcomes or a local population estimate. Bullying is a defined indicator, not a numerical measure of hate. No fashion-specific clinical treatment percentage is asserted.

sources.title: Bullying and exclusion
sources.copy: UNESCO reports that bullying affects around one pupil in three worldwide each month.

sources.title: Anxiety / depression
sources.copy: WHO estimates anxiety disorders in 5.3% and depression in 3.4% of adolescents aged 15–19 worldwide. These are separate estimates, not a combined total.

sources.title: Studies in an arts review
sources.copy: WHO’s 2019 scoping review brought together evidence from more than 3,000 studies on arts, health and wellbeing across the lifespan. It covered varied study designs and activities.

interpretation: Creative activity can offer opportunities for expression and connection. Fashion is one HTAFL route into identity and making. The broad arts evidence does not establish that fashion participation treats depression or anxiety, and these figures do not measure HTAFL’s impact.

fashionEvidence.title: Fashion and wellbeing
fashionEvidence.copy: A 2025 study of 710 Brazilian women reported both positive and negative associations between fashion clothing involvement and mental health. This cross-sectional survey cannot establish a treatment effect or be generalized to every young person.
